“I look at Trump’s coalition and I say, I’m not sure where Vice President Vance doesn’t shrink that coalition,” Shapiro said during an appearance on NPR’s podcast, “Newsmakers,” shared on Thursday.

“If you’re building a coalition, basically you have a set of knobs that turn up and down for the vice president,” the Daily Wire co-founder added. “I see pretty much all the Trump knobs turn down.”

“Obviously I think the secretary of state is far more electable than the vice president,” Shapiro added of former Florida Sen. Marco Rubio. “I don’t know if he would win, but I know his coalition would look different.”

Part of his criticism of Vance stems from Shapiro’s view that he is “extraordinarily online.”

“I think the vice president spends an inordinate amount of time worrying what the podcast bros think, like the Tucker Carlsons,” he said. “And I think that he steers directly into that.”

Shapiro thinks Vance’s “entire affect” has been “designed to appeal to 21-year-old Joe Rogan listeners.”

“And I think that that is not how you win a broad-scale national election,” he explained.

Andrew Schulz, a podcaster and comedian often grouped with the “podcast bro” tribe, also recently denounced Trump in a scathing rebuke on his show, “Brilliant Idiots,” which he co-hosts with Charlemagne tha God.

“It’s the greatest failure of a president of our lifetime,” Schulz said of the man he once voted for and platformed on his podcast. He added that Trump has had “the greatest fall from grace, miscalculation, the greatest failure.”

While it can feel like most politicians make promises they can’t keep, Schulz said, “What is more rare is literally doing the exact opposite of the things that you campaign on, to a level that nobody’s seen before and a level of corruption and cronyism that has never been seen in Western democracy.”
